what_happened: While working on a code request, Athena reached a point in reading 1 where it needed to know how page quality should be judged before shipping. Neither the repository nor the defaults answered this, so it asked the reader. The reader answered: use a model as a fresh reader with no part in building the page. That reader rates the page as a newcomer and blocks shipping below 4 of 5. Mechanical checks can sit alongside. The event was logged as a correction, but it was really an answered question.
cause: The system has no default for how to verify subjective quality such as how clear a page is to a newcomer. Requests state the outcome without a verification method. Athena's reading step does not require an acceptance check for such outcomes, so the gap only appears during the job and a person has to settle it.
prevention: Add a standing default: when a deliverable is a page or document whose quality is subjective, the acceptance check is an independent model reader that had no part in building it. It reads as a newcomer, rates the page 1 to 5, and blocks shipping below 4. Mechanical checks such as links, build and formatting may run alongside. The reading step should state this check as an acceptance criterion without asking, unless the request says otherwise.
proposed_request: Add a default to Athena's acceptance rules. For any job that delivers a page or document judged on subjective quality, the reading must include this acceptance criterion. A fresh model reader that took no part in building the work reads it as a newcomer and rates it from 1 to 5. Shipping is blocked below 4. Mechanical checks such as links, build and formatting may run alongside but do not replace the rating. The reader must be a separate invocation with no access to the builder's reasoning. Athena should apply this without asking, unless the request names a different method. Show the default in the reading of a new page-building job to confirm it appears as a criterion.
